title: prefill-decode-chunked-speculative-stage-overlap-kernel-scheduler-kv-cache-optimizations
author: Maya Chen
description: Context: This PR continues the prefill vs decode pipeline work to reduce latency and token cost for long-context workloads. It combines three complementary approaches: 1) chunked prefill (split large prefill inputs into smaller GPU-friendly chunks and overlap their KV build with decode stages), 2) speculative prefill/prefetching (kick off speculative KV buildup for likely next chunks while decode is in-flight), and 3) stage overlap with a kernel-aware scheduler and KV cache improvements. The changes aim to increase GPU utilization, lower P95 latency on mixed prefill+decode requests, and reduce per-token cost without degrading tail quality. Changes: - Runtime: add a kernel scheduler that selects optimized attention kernels based on chunk size, sequence-length histogram, and hardware topology; scheduler hooks into existing kernel selection path. - Prefill: implement chunked prefill mode with configurable chunk size and overlap window; add speculative prefill trigger heuristics (token-threshold, model confidence heuristics) and a lightweight speculative KV prefetch queue. - KV cache: introduce sharded KV cache lookups to allow parallel warmups, add LRU tuning for chunked workloads, and prefetch path improvements to avoid blocking on cold KV reads. - Batching: continuous batching changes to respect chunk boundaries and speculative prefetch priorities; ensure batching latency SLOs preserved by backpressure heuristics. - Controls & flags: add runtime flags: --enable-chunked-prefill, --chunk-size, --speculative-prefetch, and a canary rollout config for canary bandwidth limits. - Tests & tooling: microbench harness updates, new perf dashboards, and canary routing config for staged rollout. Benchmarks (internal, Cassandra long-context eval, NVLink DGX-2 equivalent): - End-to-end P50 latency: -6% on mixed prefill+decode workloads. - End-to-end P95 latency: -18% for requests with >8k prefill tokens. - Throughput (tokens/sec): +12% for sustained decode-heavy workloads. - GPU utilization on prefill-heavy tiers: +15% median, reduced variance at tails. - Estimated per-token GPU cost reduction: ~16% for large-context workloads after tuning. Backwards compatibility: chunked/speculative modes are opt-in. Default behavior unchanged. Rollout plan: staged canary (5% traffic) for 48h with fallbacks to the previous kernel selection path and ability to disable speculative prefetch remotely. Linear: ENG-1423 (kernel scheduler), ENG-1499 (chunked prefill), ENG-1512 (kv-cache improvements). Checklist: - [x] Kernel scheduler integration and unit tests - [x] Chunked prefill implementation and microbench - [x] Speculative prefetch heuristics and safety limits - [x] KV cache sharding + eviction tuning - [x] Integration tests and perf dashboards - [x] Canary config and rollback path Testing: unit tests, microbench harness, integration tests on dedicated canary fleet, end-to-end perf runs. CI: required flaky integration job rerun twice before passing. Notes: This PR is intentionally conservative about correctness changes; speculative prefetch is throttled and can be disabled per-customer. See linked commits for incremental refactors and test coverage.
